title: Model Binding Overview
description: Understand how ASP.NET Core automatically converts incoming HTTP request data into .NET objects you can work with in your controllers.

blocks.text: Every time a browser sends data to your web app, that data arrives as raw text inside an HTTP request. Model binding is the ASP.NET Core feature that reads that raw text and turns it into a strongly typed C# object so your action method can work with it directly.

Think of it like a form translator. The browser sends names and values; model binding matches those names to properties on your class and fills them in automatically. You do not have to manually read query strings, parse form fields, or convert strings to numbers.

blocks.title: A Simple Analogy
blocks.text: Imagine a restaurant order form. The waiter (the HTTP request) brings a list of items. Model binding is the kitchen staff member who reads the form and puts each item on the correct plate (your C# object) without you having to sort through the paper.

When a request arrives at a controller action, ASP.NET Core looks at the action's parameters. For each parameter that is a complex type, the framework searches the request for values with matching names. It checks route data, query string values, and form fields (in that order) until it finds a match.

If the action parameter is a simple type like int or string, model binding tries to get the value from the route data or query string. If it is a complex type like a Product or RegisterViewModel, model binding recursively binds every public property that has a matching name in the request.

Consider a registration form that collects a user's email and password. Instead of writing code to extract each field, you can accept a single view model as the action parameter and let the framework populate it.

blocks.title: RegisterViewModel with Data Annotations
blocks.content: This view model represents the data we expect from the registration form.

blocks.text: When the browser submits a POST request with form fields named Email and Password, ASP.NET Core creates a new RegisterViewModel instance, sets its properties, and passes it to the Register action. If the values cannot be converted (for example, an empty string for an integer property), model binding adds a model state error automatically.

blocks.title: Benefits of Model Binding
items: Reduces boilerplate code for reading request data
Works with many input sources automatically (route, query, form, body)
Integrates cleanly with validation attributes and ModelState
Makes controller actions easier to read and test
Handles type conversion and culture-aware parsing

blocks.title: Tip: Trust, but Verify
blocks.text: Model binding does not automatically validate your data. It only converts and populates values. Always check ModelState.IsValid before processing user input.

By default, model binding looks in several places for each parameter. The order for complex types is: form data, then the request body. For simple types, it checks route values and the query string. You can change this behavior with binding source attributes like [FromBody] or [FromQuery], which we cover in the next lesson.

terms.definition: The ASP.NET Core process that reads incoming request data and populates action method parameters or model properties.
A variable defined in a controller action method that receives bound data from the request.
A dictionary that holds the state of the model after binding and validation, including any conversion errors.
A simple class used to carry data between the client and the server, often used as the target for model binding.
The location from which model binding reads a value, such as the route, query string, form, or request body.

blocks.title: Exercise: Bind a Simple Contact Form
blocks.description: Create a Razor Page that posts a contact form and observe model binding in action.
steps: Create a new Razor Page named Contact.cshtml with a page model named ContactModel.
Add properties Name, Email, and Message to the page model.
Create a form in Contact.cshtml that posts to OnPostAsync and uses asp-for attributes.
In OnPostAsync, accept a ContactViewModel parameter and inspect ModelState.IsValid.
Run the app, submit valid and invalid data, and verify that bound values appear in the debugger.
blocks.expectedOutcome: You will see the framework populate your view model from form data and report validation errors through ModelState.

items.text: I can explain what model binding does in one sentence.
items.hint: It converts request data into .NET objects for action parameters.

items.text: I know which request parts model binding checks by default.
items.hint: Route, query string, form fields, and request body.

items.text: I can create a simple view model and bind it to a POST action.
items.hint: Use a class with properties that match form field names.

items.text: I understand the difference between ModelState.IsValid and a successful bind.
items.hint: Binding populates values; validation checks whether those values meet rules.

blocks.title: Summary
points: Model binding automatically turns HTTP request data into .NET objects.
It saves you from manually parsing query strings, form fields, and route values.
Complex types are bound from form data or the request body by default.
Simple types are bound from route data or the query string by default.
ModelState tracks binding and validation errors for the current request.
blocks.takeaway: Model binding is the bridge between the raw HTTP world and your strongly typed C# code. Mastering it makes your controllers cleaner and your forms easier to build.
